bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version

through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

=== ./.github/workflows/web.yml
# Workflow to build your docs with oranda (and mdbook)
# and deploy them to Github Pages
name: Web

# We're going to push to the gh-pages branch, so we need that permission
permissions:
  contents: write

# What situations do we want to build docs in?
# All of these work independently and can be removed / commented out
# if you don't want oranda/mdbook running in that situation
on:
  # Check that a PR didn't break docs!
  #
  # Note that the "Deploy to Github Pages" step won't run in this mode,
  # so this won't have any side-effects. But it will tell you if a PR
  # completely broke oranda/mdbook. Sadly we don't provide previews (yet)!
  pull_request:

  # Whenever something gets pushed to main, update the docs!
  # This is great for getting docs changes live without cutting a full release.
  #
  # Note that if you're using cargo-dist, this will "race" the Release workflow
  # that actually builds the Github Release that oranda tries to read (and
  # this will almost certainly complete first). As a result you will publish
  # docs for the latest commit but the oranda landing page won't know about
  # the latest release. The workflow_run trigger below will properly wait for
  # cargo-dist, and so this half-published state will only last for ~10 minutes.
  #
  # If you only want docs to update with releases, disable this, or change it to
  # a "release" branch. You can, of course, also manually trigger a workflow run
  # when you want the docs to update.
  push:
    branches:
      - main

  # Whenever a workflow called "Release" completes, update the docs!
  #
  # If you're using cargo-dist, this is recommended, as it will ensure that
  # oranda always sees the latest release right when it's available. Note
  # however that Github's UI is wonky when you use workflow_run, and won't
  # show this workflow as part of any commit. You have to go to the "actions"
  # tab for your repo to see this one running (the gh-pages deploy will also
  # only show up there).
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [ "Release" ]
    types:
      - completed

# Alright, let's do it!
jobs:
  web:
    name: Build and deploy site and docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Setup
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      # If you use any mdbook plugins, here's the place to install them!

      # Install and run oranda (and mdbook)!
      #
      # This will write all output to ./public/ (including copying mdbook's output to there).
      - name: Install and run oranda
        run: |
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/axodotdev/oranda/releases/download/v0.6.1/oranda-installer.sh | sh
          oranda build
      
      - name: Prepare HTML for link checking
        # untitaker/hyperlink supports no site prefixes, move entire site into
        # a subfolder
        run: mkdir /tmp/public/ && cp -R public /tmp/public/oranda

      - name: Check HTML for broken internal links
        uses: untitaker/hyperlink@0.1.29
        with:
          args: /tmp/public/
      
      # Deploy to our gh-pages branch (creating it if it doesn't exist).
      # The "public" dir that oranda made above will become the root dir
      # of this branch.
      #
      # Note that once the gh-pages branch exists, you must
      # go into repo's settings > pages and set "deploy from branch: gh-pages".
      # The other defaults work fine.
      - name: Deploy to Github Pages
        uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.4.1
        # ONLY if we're on main (so no PRs or feature branches allowed!)
        if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
        with:
          branch: gh-pages
          # Gotta tell the action where to find oranda's output
          folder: public
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Workflow to build your docs with oranda (and mdbook)
# and deploy them to Github Pages
name: Web

# We're going to push to the gh-pages branch, so we need that permission
permissions:
  contents: write

# What situations do we want to build docs in?
# All of these work independently and can be removed / commented out
# if you don't want oranda/mdbook running in that situation
on:
  # Check that a PR didn't break docs!
  #
  # Note that the "Deploy to Github Pages" step won't run in this mode,
  # so this won't have any side-effects. But it will tell you if a PR
  # completely broke oranda/mdbook. Sadly we don't provide previews (yet)!
  pull_request:

  # Whenever something gets pushed to main, update the docs!
  # This is great for getting docs changes live without cutting a full release.
  #
  # Note that if you're using cargo-dist, this will "race" the Release workflow
  # that actually builds the Github Release that oranda tries to read (and
  # this will almost certainly complete first). As a result you will publish
  # docs for the latest commit but the oranda landing page won't know about
  # the latest release. The workflow_run trigger below will properly wait for
  # cargo-dist, and so this half-published state will only last for ~10 minutes.
  #
  # If you only want docs to update with releases, disable this, or change it to
  # a "release" branch. You can, of course, also manually trigger a workflow run
  # when you want the docs to update.
  push:
    branches:
      - main

  # Whenever a workflow called "Release" completes, update the docs!
  #
  # If you're using cargo-dist, this is recommended, as it will ensure that
  # oranda always sees the latest release right when it's available. Note
  # however that Github's UI is wonky when you use workflow_run, and won't
  # show this workflow as part of any commit. You have to go to the "actions"
  # tab for your repo to see this one running (the gh-pages deploy will also
  # only show up there).
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [ "Release" ]
    types:
      - completed

# Alright, let's do it!
jobs:
  web:
    name: Build and deploy site and docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Setup
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      # If you use any mdbook plugins, here's the place to install them!

      # Install and run oranda (and mdbook)!
      #
      # This will write all output to ./public/ (including copying mdbook's output to there).
      - name: Install and run oranda
        run: |
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/axodotdev/oranda/releases/download/v0.6.1/oranda-installer.sh | sh
          oranda build
      
      # Deploy to our gh-pages branch (creating it if it doesn't exist).
      # The "public" dir that oranda made above will become the root dir
      # of this branch.
      #
      # Note that once the gh-pages branch exists, you must
      # go into repo's settings > pages and set "deploy from branch: gh-pages".
      # The other defaults work fine.
      - name: Deploy to Github Pages
        uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.4.1
        # ONLY if we're on main (so no PRs or feature branches allowed!)
        if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
        with:
          branch: gh-pages
          # Gotta tell the action where to find oranda's output
          folder: public
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          single-commit: true=== gitignore exists?

    /// Writes argument's help to the wrapped stream.
    fn help(
        &mut self,
        arg: Option<&Arg>,
        about: &StyledStr,
        spec_vals: &str,
        next_line_help: bool,
        longest: usize,
    ) {
        debug!("HelpTemplate::help");
        use std::fmt::Write as _;
        let literal = &self.styles.get_literal();

        // Is help on next line, if so then indent
        if next_line_help {
            debug!("HelpTemplate::help: Next Line...{next_line_help:?}");
            self.writer.push_str("\n");
            self.writer.push_str(TAB);
            self.writer.push_str(NEXT_LINE_INDENT);
        }

        let spaces = if next_line_help {
            TAB.len() + NEXT_LINE_INDENT.len()
        } else {
            longest + TAB_WIDTH * 2
        };
        let trailing_indent = spaces; // Don't indent any further than the first line is indented
        let trailing_indent = self.get_spaces(trailing_indent);

        let mut help = about.clone();
        let mut help_is_empty = help.is_empty();
        help.replace_newline_var();

        let next_line_specs = self.use_long && arg.is_some();
        if !spec_vals.is_empty() && !next_line_specs {
            if !help_is_empty {
                let sep = " ";
                help.push_str(sep);
            }
            help.push_str(spec_vals);
            help_is_empty = help.is_empty();
        }

        let avail_chars = self.term_w.saturating_sub(spaces);
        debug!(
            "HelpTemplate::help: help_width={}, spaces={}, avail={}",
            spaces,
            help.display_width(),
            avail_chars
        );
        help.wrap(avail_chars);
        help.indent("", &trailing_indent);
        self.writer.push_styled(&help);

        let mut has_possible_values = false;
        if let Some(arg) = arg {
            if !arg.is_hide_possible_values_set() && self.use_long_pv(arg) {
                const DASH_SPACE: usize = "- ".len();
                let possible_vals = arg.get_possible_values();
                if !possible_vals.is_empty() {
                    debug!("HelpTemplate::help: Found possible vals...{possible_vals:?}");
                    has_possible_values = true;

                    let longest = possible_vals
                        .iter()
                        .filter(|f| !f.is_hide_set())
                        .map(|f| display_width(f.get_name()))
                        .max()
                        .expect("Only called with possible value");

                    let spaces = spaces + TAB_WIDTH - DASH_SPACE;
                    let trailing_indent = spaces + DASH_SPACE;
                    let trailing_indent = self.get_spaces(trailing_indent);

                    if !help_is_empty {
                        let _ = write!(self.writer, "\n\n{:spaces$}", "");
                    }
                    self.writer.push_str("Possible values:");
                    for pv in possible_vals.iter().filter(|pv| !pv.is_hide_set()) {
                        let name = pv.get_name();

                        let mut descr = StyledStr::new();
                        let _ = write!(&mut descr, "{literal}{name}{literal:#}",);
                        if let Some(help) = pv.get_help() {
                            debug!("HelpTemplate::help: Possible Value help");
                            // To align help messages
                            let padding = longest - display_width(name);
                            let _ = write!(&mut descr, ": {:padding$}", "");
                            descr.push_styled(help);
                        }

                        let avail_chars = if self.term_w > trailing_indent.len() {
                            self.term_w - trailing_indent.len()
                        } else {
                            usize::MAX
                        };
                        descr.replace_newline_var();
                        descr.wrap(avail_chars);
                        descr.indent("", &trailing_indent);

                        let _ = write!(self.writer, "\n{:spaces$}- ", "",);
                        self.writer.push_styled(&descr);
                    }
                }
            }
        }

        if !spec_vals.is_empty() && next_line_specs {
            let mut help = StyledStr::new();
            if !help_is_empty || has_possible_values {
                let sep = "\n\n";
                help.push_str(sep);
            }
            help.push_str(spec_vals);

            help.wrap(avail_chars);
            help.indent("", &trailing_indent);
            self.writer.push_styled(&help);
        }
    }

    fn write_args(&mut self, args: &[&Arg], _category: &str, sort_key: ArgSortKey) {
        debug!("HelpTemplate::write_args {_category}");
        // The shortest an arg can legally be is 2 (i.e. '-x')
        let mut longest = 2;
        let mut ord_v = BTreeMap::new();

        // Determine the longest
        for &arg in args.iter().filter(|arg| {
            // If it's NextLineHelp we don't care to compute how long it is because it may be
            // NextLineHelp on purpose simply *because* it's so long and would throw off all other
            // args alignment
            should_show_arg(self.use_long, arg)
        }) {
            let width = display_width(&arg.to_string());
            let actual_width = if arg.get_long().is_some() {
                width + SHORT_SIZE
            } else {
                width
            };
            longest = longest.max(actual_width);
            debug!(
                "HelpTemplate::write_args: arg={:?} longest={}",
                arg.get_id(),
                longest
            );

            let key = (sort_key)(arg);
            ord_v.insert(key, arg);
        }

        let next_line_help = self.will_args_wrap(args, longest);

        for (i, (_, arg)) in ord_v.iter().enumerate() {
            if i != 0 {
                self.writer.push_str("\n");
                if next_line_help && self.use_long {

                }

            self.write_arg(arg, next_line_help, longest);
        }
    }

    /// Writes help for an argument to the wrapped stream.
    fn write_arg(&mut self, arg: &Arg, next_line_help: bool, longest: usize) {
        let spec_vals = &self.spec_vals(arg);

        self.writer.push_str(TAB);
        self.short(arg);
        self.long(arg);
        self.writer
            .push_styled(&arg.stylize_arg_suffix(self.styles, None));
        self.align_to_about(arg, next_line_help, longest);

        let about = if self.use_long {
            arg.get_long_help()
                .or_else(|| arg.get_help())
                .unwrap_or_default()
        } else {
            arg.get_help()
                .or_else(|| arg.get_long_help())
                .unwrap_or_default()
        };

        self.help(Some(arg), about, spec_vals, next_line_help, longest);
    }

    /// Writes argument's short command to the wrapped stream.
    fn short(&mut self, arg: &Arg) {
        debug!("HelpTemplate::short");
        use std::fmt::Write as _;
        let literal = &self.styles.get_literal();

        if let Some(s) = arg.get_short() {
            let _ = write!(self.writer, "{literal}-{s}{literal:#}",);
        } else if arg.get_long().is_some() {
            self.writer.push_str("    ");
        }
    }

    /// Writes argument's long command to the wrapped stream.
    fn long(&mut self, arg: &Arg) {
        debug!("HelpTemplate::long");
        use std::fmt::Write as _;
        let literal = &self.styles.get_literal();

        if let Some(long) = arg.get_long() {
            if arg.get_short().is_some() {
                self.writer.push_str(", ");
            }
            let _ = write!(self.writer, "{literal}--{long}{literal:#}",);
        }
    }

pub(crate) fn dimensions() -> (Option<usize>, Option<usize>) {
    #[cfg(not(feature = "wrap_help"))]
    return (None, None);

    #[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
    terminal_size::terminal_size()

}

#[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
fn parse_env(var: &str) -> Option<usize> {
    some!(some!(std::env::var_os(var)).to_str())
        .parse::<usize>()
        .ok()
}

fn should_show_arg(use_long: bool, arg: &Arg) -> bool {
    debug!(
        "should_show_arg: use_long={:?}, arg={}",
        use_long,
        arg.get_id()
    );
    if arg.is_hide_set() {
        return false;
    }
    (!arg.is_hide_long_help_set() && use_long)
        || (!arg.is_hide_short_help_set() && !use_long)
        || arg.is_next_line_help_set()
}

/// Returns the size of the terminal attached to stdout.
pub fn terminal_size() -> Option<(Width, Height)> {
    let mut winsize = Winsize::default();
    let result = unsafe { ioctl(1, TIOCGWINSZ, &mut winsize as *mut Winsize) };
    if result == -1 {
        return None;
    }
    if winsize.ws_col == 0 && winsize.ws_row == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    Some((Width(winsize.ws_col), Height(winsize.ws_row)))

    fn arg_next_line_help(&self, arg: &Arg, spec_vals: &str, longest: usize) -> bool {
        if self.next_line_help || arg.is_next_line_help_set() || self.use_long {
            // setting_next_line
            true
        } else {
            // force_next_line
            let h = arg
                .get_help()
                .or_else(|| arg.get_long_help())
                .unwrap_or_default();
            let h_w = h.display_width() + display_width(spec_vals);
            let taken = longest + TAB_WIDTH * 2;
            self.term_w >= taken
                && (taken as f32 / self.term_w as f32) > 0.40
                && h_w > (self.term_w - taken)
        }
    }

import json, subprocess, os, shutil, sys

cases = [
  '{"foo": 1}',

]

    err = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','build','--json-only'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stderr
    diag = None
    for line in out.split('\n'):
        if line.startswith('{'):
            diag = json.loads(line)['diagnostic']; break
    lines = [l for l in err.split('\n') if l.startswith('  \u2570') or (l.startswith('      ') and not l.startswith('   '))]
    if not diag: print("no diag for", cfg); continue
    for ci, cause in enumerate(diag['causes']):
        # find the rendered lines for this cause: those starting with "  \u2570\u2500\u25b6 " or continuation "      "

        for l in err.split('\n'):
            if l.startswith('  \u2570\u2500\u25b6 '):
                if started: break
                started = True
                rendered.append(l[6:])
            elif started and l.startswith('      ') and not l.startswith('      \u'):
                rendered.append(l[6:])
            elif started:
                break
        text = cause
        # feasible width for this cause: each rendered line is a greedy break
        for ridx, r in enumerate(rendered):
            # r must be a prefix-based break; compute constraints
            # find where r ends in the remaining text
            if not text.startswith(r):
                print("MISMATCH", cfg, ci, ridx, repr(r), repr(text[:50])); break
            rest = text[len(r):]
            if rest == '':
                continue
            # next word after the break
            stripped = rest.lstrip(' ')
            sep = len(rest) - len(stripped)
            nxt = stripped.split(' ')[0]
            lo = max(lo, len(r))
            hi = min(hi, len(r) + sep + len(nxt) - 1)
            text = stripped
    print(f"after {cfg!r}: W in [{lo}, {hi}]")
print("FINAL W in [%d, %d]" % (lo, hi))

import json, subprocess, os, shutil

cases = [
  '{"foo": 1}',
  '{"styles": {"syntax_theme": "zzz"}}',
  '{"styles": {"theme": "axo"}}',
  '{"workspace": {"members": [{"slug": 123456}]}}',
  '{"workspace": {"members": ["averylongstring"]}}',
  '{"marketing": {"analytics": {"google": {}}}}',
  '{"project": {"name": true}}',
]
lo, hi = 1, 10000
def rendered_causes(err):
    lines = err.split('\n')
    groups = []
    cur = None
    for l in lines:
        if l.startswith('  \u2570\u2500\u25b6 '):
            cur = [l[6:]]
            groups.append(cur)
        elif cur is not None and l.startswith('      '):
            cur.append(l[6:])
        elif cur is not None:
            break
    return groups
for cfg in cases:
    d = '/tmp/wb'
    shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    open(d+'/oranda.json','w').write(cfg)
    out = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','--output-format','json','build','--json-only'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
    err = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','build','--json-only'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True).stderr
    diag = None
    for line in out.split('\n'):
        if line.startswith('{'):
            diag = json.loads(line)['diagnostic']; break
    if not diag:
        print("no diag", cfg); continue
    groups = rendered_causes(err)
    for ci, cause in enumerate(diag['causes']):
        if ci >= len(groups): break
        text = cause
        for r in groups[ci]:
            if not text.startswith(r):
                print("MISMATCH", cfg, repr(r[:40]), repr(text[:40])); break
            rest = text[len(r):]
            if rest == '': break
            stripped = rest.lstrip(' ')
            sep = len(rest) - len(stripped)
            nxt = stripped.split(' ')[0]
            lo = max(lo, len(r)); hi = min(hi, len(r) + sep + len(nxt) - 1)
            text = stripped
    print("%-50s W in [%d, %d]" % (cfg, lo, hi))
print("FINAL W in [%d, %d]" % (lo, hi))
PYEOF"}

/// Render a block of text with a prefix on the first line and a different
/// prefix on every continuation line.
fn block(text: &str, width: usize, first: &str, cont: &str) -> String {
    let lines = wrap_text(text, width);
    let mut out = String::new();
    for (idx, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {

import subprocess, shutil, os, json
def analyze(c, patlen=9, reps=12):
    d = '/tmp/wv'; shutil.rmtree(d, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(d)
    v = (c + 'a'*patlen) * reps
    open(d+'/oranda.json','w').write(json.dumps({'styles': {'oranda_css_version': v}}))
    r = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','build'], cwd=d, capture_output=True, text=True)
    lines = r.stderr.split('\n')
    # message line and continuation
    msg = "error sending request for url (https://octolotl.axodotdev.host/downloads/axodotdev/oranda/%s/oranda.css): error trying to connect: dns error: failed to lookup address information: Temporary failure in name resolution" % v
    rendered = []
    started = False
    for l in lines:
        if l.startswith('  \u00d7 '):
            started = True; rendered.append(l[4:])
        elif started and l.startswith('  \u2502 '):
            rendered.append(l[4:])
        elif started:
            break
    pos = 0
    out = []
    for rl in rendered:
        if not msg.startswith(rl, pos):
            out.append("MISMATCH at %d" % pos); break
        pos += len(rl)
        nxt = msg[pos:pos+1]
        prev = msg[pos-1]
        out.append("brk after %r (idx %d) next=%r" % (prev, pos-1, nxt))
    print("char %r:" % c, out)
for c in ['/', '-', '.', '_', ':', '=']:
    analyze(c)
PYEOF"}

```rust
}
```

```rust
fn wrap_line(line: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = line.chars().collect();
    let n = chars.len();
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut pos = 0usize;
    loop {
        if pos >= n { break; }
        let remaining = n - pos;
        if remaining <= width {
            out.push(chars[pos..].iter().collect::<String>().trim_end().to_string());  // hmm, trim_end?
            break;
        }
        // find the last break opportunity <= pos + width
        let limit = pos + width;
        let mut best: Option<usize> = None;
        for i in (pos + 1)..=limit {
            let after = if i < n { chars[i] } else { ' ' };
            if can_break(chars[i-1], after) { best = Some(i); }
        }
        match best {
            Some(p) => {
                let mut end = p;
                while end > pos && chars[end-1].is_whitespace() { end -= 1; }
                out.push(chars[pos..end].iter().collect());
                let mut next = p;
                while next < n && chars[next].is_whitespace() { next += 1; }
                pos = next;
            }
            None => {
                let end = limit;
                out.push(chars[pos..end].iter().collect());
                pos = end;
            }
        }
    }
    out
}
```

```rust
fn wrap_line(line: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = line.chars().collect();
    let n = chars.len();
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut pos = 0usize;
    loop {
        if pos >= n { break; }
        let remaining = n - pos;
        if remaining <= width {
            out.push(chars[pos..].iter().collect::<String>().trim_end().to_string());  // hmm, trim_end?
            break;
        }
        // find the last break opportunity <= pos + width
        let limit = pos + width;
        let mut best: Option<usize> = None;
        for i in (pos + 1)..=limit {
            let after = if i < n { chars[i] } else { ' ' };
            if can_break(chars[i-1], after) { best = Some(i); }
        }
        match best {
            Some(p) => {
                let mut end = p;
                while end > pos && chars[end-1].is_whitespace() { end -= 1; }
                out.push(chars[pos..end].iter().collect());
                let mut next = p;
                while next < n && chars[next].is_whitespace() { next += 1; }
                pos = next;
            }
            None => {
                let end = limit;
                out.push(chars[pos..end].iter().collect());
                pos = end;
            }
        }
    }
    out
}
```

```rust
    let chars: Vec<char> = line.chars().collect();
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut pos = 0usize;   // char index
    loop {
        if pos >= chars.len() { break }
        // find the last break opportunity <= pos + width
        let limit = (pos + width).min(chars.len());
        let mut best: Option<usize> = None;
        for i in (pos + 1)..=limit {
```

```rust
fn wrap_line(line: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = line.chars().collect();
    let n = chars.len();
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut pos = 0usize;
    loop {
        if pos >= n { break; }
        let remaining = n - pos;
        if remaining <= width {
            out.push(chars[pos..].iter().collect::<String>().trim_end().to_string());  // hmm, trim_end?
            break;
        }
        // find the last break opportunity <= pos + width
        let limit = pos + width;
        let mut best: Option<usize> = None;
        for i in (pos + 1)..=limit {
            let after = if i < n { chars[i] } else { ' ' };
            if can_break(chars[i-1], after) { best = Some(i); }
        }
        match best {
            Some(p) => {
                let mut end = p;
                while end > pos && chars[end-1].is_whitespace() { end -= 1; }
                out.push(chars[pos..end].iter().collect());
                let mut next = p;
                while next < n && chars[next].is_whitespace() { next += 1; }
                pos = next;
            }
            None => {
                let end = limit;
                out.push(chars[pos..end].iter().collect());
                pos = end;
            }
        }
    }
    out
}
```

```rust
fn wrap_line(line: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
    let chars: Vec<char> = line.chars().collect();
    let n = chars.len();
    let mut out: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

        let mut best: Option<usize> = None;
        for i in (pos + 1)..=limit {
            let after = if i < n { chars[i] } else { ' ' };
            if can_break(chars[i-1], after) { best = Some(i); }

                while end > pos && chars[end-1].is_whitespace() { end -= 1; }

                pos = next;
            }
            None => {
                let end = limit;
                out.push(chars[pos..end].iter().collect());
                pos = end;
            }
        }
    }
    out
}
```

## What this is

A from-scratch Rust re-implementation of `oranda 0.6.5` (axo.dev static-site
generator), written only from observed behaviour of the provided
`./executable` (no source, no disassembly, no network).

Build: `./compile.sh` (uses `cargo build --release --offline`, then copies

```
Cargo.toml            clap 4.6.1 (+wrap_help), serde, serde_json, indexmap
vendor/terminal_size/ shim crate so clap's `wrap_help` feature can compile offline
assets/favicon.ico    default favicon (bytes captured from the original's output)
assets/livereload.js  tower-livereload script (captured from the original's output)
assets/web.yml.template, assets/link_check.yml   `generate ci` templates
src/cli.rs            clap Command tree (help output verified byte-identical)
src/diag.rs           miette-style graphical + JSON diagnostic renderer
src/config.rs         oranda.json schema (serde, deny_unknown_fields)
src/log.rs            `ââ >o_o< INFO:` style logging
src/http_client.rs    DNS/TCP/TLS(openssl) client used to fetch oranda.css
src/http_server.rs    hyper+tower-http-like file server (serve/dev)
src/httpdate.rs, src/mime.rs, src/term.rs, src/watch.rs, src/prompt.rs
src/project.rs        `cargo metadata --no-deps` project detection
src/commands/{build,dev,serve,generate}.rs
src/main.rs           dispatch, config loading, exit codes
```

  40/80/120/200/300 and via the `COLUMNS` fallback (width 100 when piped)

  subcommand/argument/value, suggestions, invalid port)

  `X` to build your project in.` + `Not a directory (os error 20)` paths
* `build`: project-detection warning (cargo metadata failure, exact cause
  chain), `public/favicon.ico`, the oranda.css fetch attempt with the
  `Fetching from proxy encountered an error:` / `Falling back to GitHub
  directly...` messages and the reqwest-shaped error chain (exit 255)
* config parse diagnostics: serde_json messages, miette snippet rendering
  (`ââ[./oranda.json:L:C]`, gutter widths, underline placement), JSON
  diagnostic objects (message/severity/causes/help/filename/labels/related)
* `serve`: 200/206/304/307/400/404/405/416/500 responses, header order, range
  rules (incl. multipart 416 body), `If-Modified-Since`, mime table,
  directory redirect + index.html, percent decoding, NUL path 500
* `dev`: watch-path derivation & normalisation, `Found N paths to watch`,
  `Files watched: [...]`, livereload injection, livereload endpoints,
  `Path(s) [...] changed, rebuilding...`, rebuild loop, BuildNotFound panic
* `generate ci`: non-TTY panic (`src/generate.rs:56:14`) and the full TTY
  dialoguer interaction (ANSI sequences byte-identical) incl. produced files
* diagnostic wrapping width (118; message prefix 4 â 114, cause prefix 6 â 112)

## Known gaps / TODO

1. **Line-break rule set is approximate.** The original breaks lines at
   Unicode line-break opportunities. Empirically established: break after
   whitespace, after `/ - ? ! | }`; never break before `. : , ; ' ) ] `
   digits; a break before whitespace is always allowed; unbreakable runs are
   hard-broken at exactly the wrap width. This matches all realistic inputs
   (config errors, URLs, cargo diagnostics) but still differs for text with
   dense ASCII punctuation. Failing cases are saved by the randomised
   comparison harness (`/tmp/runall.sh`, `cmp.sh`, `cmp_http.sh`,
   `cmp_dev.sh`, `cmp_tty.sh` in /tmp). Next step: probe the remaining
   characters with the controlled field-name harness used in the trace
   (field name = `'a'*90 + C + 'a'*200` â break-after, `'a'*98 + C + â¦` â
   break-before) and extend `breaks_after` / `no_break_before` in
   `src/diag.rs`.
2. **Full site build is unreachable offline** (oranda must download
   `oranda.css` over TLS first), so `src/site.rs` is a stub. If network is
   available the markdownâHTML pipeline must be written (CommonMark renderer,
   theming, mdbook support, cargo-dist artifact JSON). The fetch itself is
   implemented (openssl FFI) but untested.
3. **`build --json-only`** only creates the dist dir + success message; the
   original also builds an artifacts JSON when cargo-dist data is available
   (needs network, so unobservable here).
4. Backtrace output when `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` is set is not reproduced
   (addresses are not reproducible anyway).
5. The hyper bind-failure panic location string is hardcoded to the registry
   path the original prints.

## Harnesses (in /tmp, not committed)

`cmp.sh <name> <setup> <args...>` â compares orig vs mine (stdout, stderr,
exit code, produced files). `cmp_http.sh`, `cmp_dev.sh`, `cmp_tty.sh` cover
the server, watcher and interactive-prompt paths. `runall.sh` runs the CLI
regression suite.
EOF
git add -A && git -c user.email=a@b.c -c user.name=agent commit -q -m "Re-implement oranda 0.6.5 from observed behaviour" && git log --oneline | head -3; git status --short | head"}
